title: Release made it slow
scenario: "Since release <sha>, p95 latency went from 80 ms to 900 ms. Fix it now." — SRE pager (FEAT-07 / GD-02)
mission: Detect a latency regression from the alert, prove it is not saturation, and roll back with git revert.
objectives: Explain why the HPA does not help

prerequisites.notes: Inject chaos.latencyMs: "800" in prod through a deploy PR (you or a partner).

steps.title: Diagnose
steps.detail: CPU normal? Then not saturation; look at recent changes.

steps.title: Roll back
steps.detail: git revert of the deploy PR; Argo CD syncs.

criteria.text: p95 latency back under the SLO threshold
A revert commit of the chaos change exists on main
Time to restore recorded in the post-mortem

expectedResult: Restore in minutes with a Git audit trail.
recovery: Do not wait for the HPA: latency is not CPU-bound here.
dont: Do not scale up as the "fix"
hints: Is CPU high? If not, more pods will not help.
Argo CD history shows the last values change.
Revert the PR, not the commit on main by hand.

interview.question: Latency spiked after a release. Walk me through detection, diagnosis and rollback.
followUps: Revert vs fix forward — how do you decide?

debrief: Correlate the regression with the change timeline; revert first, investigate after. Git revert keeps the cluster and the audit trail consistent.

checker.plan: Read-only: Prometheus query via Azure Monitor workspace, git log --grep Revert, post-mortem file.

validation.notes: Checker not implemented yet; needs the observability layer.
